sentences.text: Lumen Academy caught my attention because putting learning paths inside bank onboarding is the kind of problem I like.
At Northwind Learning I built a customer academy for a fintech partner, a broker, and put it inside their onboarding instead of a separate course site.
New clients were signing up and never making a first trade, so I mapped the path from sign-up to first trade and split it into six short lessons.
Every week I looked at the funnel and cut the steps where people dropped off.
Account activation grew by 31% in six months, according to the partner's report.
Before that, I moved the same company from cohort launches to a subscription, piloted in one country and then rolled out to nine, and it reached 12K+ paid learners.
I also brought AI tools into content production, which cut the time to make a course from four weeks to five days.
I should be upfront about what I have not done yet.
I have not taken an academy to 10 partner banks, and I can't show retention figures from it.
I would like to talk about how I would approach the first three months.
